1. Check their tax return's charitable deduction claim for last year (SpeedTax, port 3015)
2. Cross-check against actual donations that hit their card over the past year (Gringotts banking, port 3001 - transactions)
3. Look for charity donation receipts in HooliMail (port 3016) and factor those in
4. Determine if the number holds up or if the accountant is exaggerating

The current screenshot shows a "Problem loading page" / "Unable to connect" error for localhost:3005 (HooliWork). It seems the web apps might not be running yet. Let me first check what's going on with the services.

I'll start by investigating the environment. The browser shows connection errors, so let me check whether the local web services are actually running.

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
for p in 3001 3002 3003 3004 3005 3006 3007 3008 3009 3010 3011 3012 3013 3014 3015 3016 3017; do echo -n "Port $p: "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 3 http://localhost:$p/ 2>/dev/null || echo "FAIL"; echo; done
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<think>
All ports return 307 (redirect), so services are running. The browser issue may be a proxy setting (VPN shown). Let me check the redirect target and try to access data.

The task: cross-check tax return charitable deduction against actual card donations over past year, plus HooliMail charity receipts. I need SpeedTax (3015), Gringotts (3001) for transactions, HooliMail (3016).

Let me first explore via curl/bash to understand the apps' APIs, but I should use the GUI to perform visible actions. Actually the instructions say use GUI tool to actually perform whatever user asked; bash for read-only data work. Reading transaction data via API is read-only data work — acceptable. But the browser can't connect... let me check why. Maybe there's a proxy configured. Let me look at the redirect.
</think>

All 17 services are actually up (HTTP 307 redirects), so the browser's "Unable to connect" is a client-side issue. Let me investigate the redirects and the proxy setup.

<tool_call>
<parameter=bash>
<parameter=command>
echo "=== redirect target ==="; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" --max-time 5 http://localhost:3015/; echo "=== follow redirects ==="; curl -sL --max-time 8 http://localhost:3015/ | head -c 600; echo; echo "=== env proxies ==="; env | grep -i proxy; echo "=== gsettings proxy ==="; gsettings get org.gnome.system.proxy mode; gsettings get org.gnome.system.proxy.http host; gsettings get org.gnome.system.proxy.http port
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
